description: Os ReCINfences is a team of Computer Engineering students from CIn-UFPE (Recife, Brazil), united by our passion for technology and, above all, the innovations NASA develops for space exploration. We are joining the NASA Space Apps Challenge to learn, collaborate, and build innovative solutions, combining software engineering, data, and creativity to tackle real challenges faced by humanity beyond Earth, from our corner of Northeast Brazil to the future of space.
summary: Lyra is a web application designed to support autonomous health monitoring for astronauts during long-duration space missions. When communication with Earth is delayed or unavailable, crew members must be able to recognize changes in their health, understand potential risks, and follow appropriate procedures without requiring medical expertise. At the core of our solution is a neural network (VEGA) developed by our team to analyze astronaut health data, helping identify patterns, physiological changes, and potential anomalies that require attention. Combined with continuous health monitoring, personalized health trends, and an intuitive interface, this technology aims to transform complex physiological data into accessible and actionable insights. A key differentiator is our female-specific health analysis, which recognizes that women may experience distinct physiological responses and health challenges during space missions. By incorporating sex-related physiological differences and female-specific health indicators, the system aims to provide more personalized monitoring, addressing gaps in traditional approaches that may overlook women's health needs. Rather than simply displaying medical data, Lyra aims to turn observations into understandable, actionable information. The project draws on NASA's Human Research Program and space biology research to explore a safer, more autonomous approach to crew health management.
details:
Lyra: Crew Care — Autonomous Health Monitoring for Deep-Space Crews

"Your health cannot wait for a signal from Earth."

Lyra: Crew Care is a web application developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 (Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions) designed to help astronauts monitor their health during long-duration space missions, including scenarios where communication with Earth is severely delayed or unavailable.

Rather than merely displaying raw measurements, the platform helps crew members understand what changed, why it matters, what can be verified, and which approved onboard procedure to consult—serving as a decision-support tool without replacing medical professionals.

The Challenge

Long-duration space missions expose crews to radiation, isolation, confinement, altered gravity, and closed environments. Health changes can emerge gradually while communication delays make synchronous consultations with ground-based specialists impractical. Solving this requires balancing three core dimensions:

  • Scientific: Interpreting measurements using individual baselines, quality checks, and proper context.
  • Operational: Ensuring critical functions work autonomously without relying on an always-available connection to Earth.
  • Human: Providing an accessible interface for non-medical crew members operating under fatigue, stress, or time pressure.

Key Differentiators

  • VEGA (Custom Neural Network): Developed by our team to analyze physiological observations and symptoms, VEGA helps uncover subtle patterns and anomalies that would be difficult to spot from isolated readings—complementing personal baselines and safety rules rather than replacing clinical judgment.
  • Individualized Female Health Analysis: Moving beyond a one-size-fits-all model, Lyra: Crew Care accounts for sex-related physiological factors and supports optional, consented tracking of female-specific health parameters whenever scientifically relevant.
  • Accessible for Non-Medical Crew: Translates complex technical outputs into clear explanations, highlighting supporting evidence, uncertainty levels, and direct references to approved onboard procedures.
  • Offline-First Architecture: Engineered to operate autonomously during communication blackouts, keeping check-ins, personal history, local guidance, and inference available onboard, with an asynchronous queue to sync reports once connectivity returns.
  • Transparent and Responsible Monitoring: Clearly separates VEGA's model outputs from rule-based safety checks, explicitly flagging missing, simulated, or uncertain data instead of treating uncertainty as normal health.

System Workflow

  1. Collect & Validate: Receives manual health check-ins or sensor readings with timestamps and units, checking for missing entries or implausible values.
  2. Contextualize & Analyze: Evaluates observations against the astronaut's personal baseline, relevant physiological context, and VEGA's neural network analysis.
  3. Explain & Guide: When an observation requires review, presents the supporting evidence, communicates uncertainty, and links directly to an approved local procedure.
  4. Preserve & Sync: Logs events locally on the device (IndexedDB/PWA) for onboard follow-up and queues reports for later transmission to Mission Control.

Technology Stack

  • Frontend & Offline Capabilities: React, TypeScript, Vite, Progressive Web App (PWA / Service Workers), and IndexedDB.
  • AI & Scientific Foundations: VEGA neural network for anomaly and pattern analysis, grounded in NASA open science resources and standards (HRP, OSDR, NLSP, and NASA Open APIs).
